newsitem.title: UK: Hague wins UK Conservative crown -- what they said.
newsitem.headline: Hague wins UK Conservative crown -- what they said.

text.p: Following are some of the reactions to William Hague's victory over Kenneth Clarke on Thursday to become leader of Britain's main opposition Conservative party.

Hague: "I see it as my job not only to lead the party but to heal its divisions. I owe it to every member of the party to make sure I extend the hand of friendship and co-operation to all members of the party."

Kenneth Clarke, explaining why he will not join Hague's "shadow" cabinet: "I have been on the front benches for 26 years. I have either been in most departments or I have shadowed them. I've retained my enthusiasm for politics and I think it might wear off if I carry on shadowing yet another department or part of government."
John Townend, a right-wing Conservative Euro-sceptic: "I think from what William has said the European schism is over. We unite behind a Euro-sceptic."
Peter Temple-Morris, a pro-European: "There are a number of us that are stuck on the beach on that particular issue."
Sir Teddy Taylor, a Hague supporter: "Lady Thatcher intervened at just the right time."
Tim Yeo, another Hague backer: "I think many people were unhappy about this deal between Ken Clarke and John Redwood."
Sir Patrick Cormack, a Clarke supporter: "We shall all unite behind the new leader. I voted for Mr Clarke, but that is all over and done with."
David Curry, who also backed Clarke: "It is much better that it should be a decisive result."
Peter Luff, a Clarke supporter: "Mr Hague will do a good job. It is up to us to treat him a bit better than we treated John Major."

Labour Trade Secretary Margaret Beckett: "Given the loathing in the party, the idea that William Hague can put together an effective team defies credibility. After this result it is clear that William Hague will forever be the prisoner of the right."

Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown: "By turning their back on Kenneth Clarke the Conservative Party have turned their back on the one person who could drag them back to moderation, common-sense and 'one nation' values."
Hague's mother, Stella: "He would make a fantastic leader, and I have supreme confidence in him. He has tremendous abilities."
